## Summary

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
I am a statistician and data scientist with more than ten years of work in R and Python. My degree is in statistics, and my thesis compared estimators of the fractional differencing parameter in long-memory series. Since then the job has mostly been getting models out of a research setting and into production, which in practice has meant PySpark, Parquet, Docker and SQL alongside the statistics.

At CIAT I spent six years modelling how climate change affects crops and other productive sectors, using probabilistic time series and state-space models, and I worked on the statistical models behind the AClimate Colombia seasonal forecasts. As part of the CIAT climate services team I shared in the 2017 UNFCCC Momentum for Change award.

Since 2021 I have worked in industry on churn, segmentation, pricing, forecasting and recommendation, and I led the data science on the DirecTV account. A churn model earns its keep when its drivers become customer segments that a marketing team can write a campaign for, so that is where I put the effort.

My publications sit mostly in climate and agriculture: seven journal articles and two reports as co-author, with 215 citations on Google Scholar. I currently work as an AI engineer at Globant, with Disney as the client, where I lead parts of the agent design on LLM systems built with LangGraph and Azure OpenAI.
:::

## Experience

### AI Engineer, Globant (client: Disney) {.cv-role dates="Dec 2025 – Present · Remote, Colombia"}

- Lead parts of the agent design on the multi-agent work, including prompt engineering and the contracts between agents.
- Designed and implemented a multi-agent system that reads a codebase and writes its documentation. Set the split between deterministic and LLM steps, and tightened the schemas agents exchange so that a bad output fails loudly instead of slipping through.
- Built a conversational intake agent for internal product requests. It pushes back on vague or solution-first input and flags overlap across teams. Product teams now spend 8 to 10 fewer hours a week on triage, and first-time completion rose from 60% to 90%.
- Built the ETL and LLM engine behind scheduled weekly executive and bi-weekly tactical reports. Live data from project-management tools goes into one reporting model under extraction rules that keep field-level provenance, and a dry-run gate with risk routing runs before anything is distributed.

Tools: Python, LangGraph, Azure OpenAI, REST APIs, Docker, Git, CI/CD.

### Senior Data Scientist, Globant {.cv-role dates="May 2021 – Dec 2025 · Remote, Colombia"}

**Sportian account** (Aug 2023 – Dec 2025)

- Built statistical and machine learning models for sports-industry products, mainly pricing and match analytics.
- Worked with time series, econometric methods and embeddings on historical sales and event data.

**Augmented Staffing, internal to Globant** (Feb 2022 – Jan 2023)

- Forecast and clustered internal staffing tickets to plan recruiting.
- Built a semantic search and recommendation tool that matched candidates to tickets on text embeddings, then added a seniority estimation model in PyTorch with an ordinal loss to improve the match. Pipelines ran on Kubeflow.

**DirecTV** (May 2021 – Dec 2021)

- Led data science on the account: subscriber segmentation for DirecTV GO, the churn model and the marketing campaign work.
- The churn model combined platform usage with sentiment from text, using custom neural networks in PyTorch. Its feature importance fed the segments.
- Retention and acquisition email campaigns drew on an econometric analysis of subscription pricing and a market basket analysis. Pipelines ran on AWS SageMaker, with data from Athena and S3.

### Professor (part-time), Universidad del Valle and Universidad Católica {.cv-role dates="Aug 2020 – Jun 2021 · Cali, Colombia"}

- Universidad del Valle: Time Series Analysis and Probability. Universidad Católica: Fundamentals of Statistics I and II.

### Data Scientist, CIAT (International Center for Tropical Agriculture) {.cv-role dates="Jan 2015 – Mar 2020 · Cali, Colombia"}

- Modelled climate variables and their effect on crops and other productive sectors with probabilistic time series models, state-space models and spatio-temporal stochastic processes.
- Worked on the statistical models behind the AClimate Colombia seasonal forecast platform ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compag.2020.105486)).
- Studied near-term climate change impacts on major crops in Latin America and the Caribbean for the IDB and USAID. Set up multiple DSSAT and ORYZA runs from R for the region's five main production systems and combined them with machine learning and geostatistics.
- Mapped climate service hotspots worldwide for USAID (2017–2018), meaning places where agro-climatic information could help close yield gaps. GAMs and other machine learning, the whole process in R ([AgMetGaps](https://ciat-dapa.github.io/AgMetGaps/)).
- Built an index with spatial machine learning models to support the breeding of climate-smart crops.
- Orinoco regional climate change plan (Meta, Casanare, Vichada and Arauca, 2015–2016): climate clusters, geospatial models automated in R, and yield simulation for eleven production systems in the Llanos.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
- Public R code I contributed to: [usaid_forecast_maize](https://github.com/CIAT-DAPA/usaid_forecast_maize) and [AgMetGaps](https://github.com/CIAT-DAPA/AgMetGaps).
:::

### Student Intern, CIAT {.cv-role dates="Apr – Oct 2014 · Cali, Colombia"}

- Classified production systems with cluster analysis for Colombia's Fondo Adaptación, with CORPOICA, as part of a vulnerability analysis for areas hit by the rainy season.

### Earlier work {.cv-role dates="2010 – 2013"}

- **Consultant, Universidad del Valle** (2012–2013): statistical design and analysis for two engineering theses, one on constructed wetlands (factorial and repeated-measures designs, mixed models), one on cubic equations of state (non-linear models, bootstrap).
- **Professor, Universidad Santiago de Cali** (2013): statistics in R for research faculty.

## Skills

**Time series and statistics:** state-space models and Kalman filters, ARIMA, GARCH, long-memory models, Gaussian processes, regression and mixed models, GAMs, experimental design, bootstrap, geostatistics.

**Machine learning:** clustering, dimensionality reduction (PCA, kernel PCA, t-SNE, UMAP), gradient boosting (XGBoost), deep learning (PyTorch), anomaly detection, scikit-learn.

**Text and LLMs:** agents and multi-agent systems (LangGraph, LangChain), prompt engineering, embeddings and vector search, topic models, Hugging Face, OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, LangSmith, PromptLayer.

**Programming:** R (advanced), Python, SQL.

**Data and cloud:** PySpark, sparklyr, Polars, pandas, Parquet, raster and satellite data, Databricks, AWS (SageMaker, Athena, S3), GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery), Azure (OpenAI, Functions, DevOps).

**Engineering:** Git, GitHub, GitLab, Docker, Kubeflow, CI/CD, DVC, Datadog, Linux, Quarto, R Markdown, LaTeX.

**Domain:** climate impact modelling, crop simulation (DSSAT, ORYZA), churn, customer segmentation, pricing.

**Languages:** Spanish (native), English (B2, upper intermediate).

## Education

**B.Sc. in Statistics**, Universidad del Valle, Cali (2008 – 2014). Thesis: *Comparison of estimation methods for the fractional differencing parameter in conditionally heteroscedastic long-memory time series.*

**Thesis supervision:** co-director of an undergraduate thesis in Statistics, Universidad del Valle (2023), *Spectral analysis of Colombian genres: La Cumbia* (in Spanish). [Open access](https://hdl.handle.net/10893/30344).

## Awards

**UNFCCC Momentum for Change award**, 2017, as part of the CIAT climate services team. **Best Research Outcome**, CIAT, 2017.
